A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

rapamycin extends mouse lifespan by 9‐15% at doses of 2.5 and 5 mg/kg/day, and by 23‐26% at a higher dose (8 mg/kg/day) that is toxic at higher doses and is also metabolically distinct from the effects of caloric restriction.

The main takeaway from our work is that
rapamycin is a promising drug for extending mouse longevity, although its efficacy may be limited by its toxicity at high dose.

rapamycin‐mediated lifespan increase is a robust phenomenon in mice that is dose‐dependent and sexually dimorphic, and that the mechanisms by which rapamycin and dietary restriction extend mouse lifespan may be quite distinct.
rapamycin is not an exact mimic of dietary restriction, but rather, it is a distinct form of dietary restriction that can be used to study mechanisms of lifespan extension in a mammalian system.
